question: Assume today is 2026-08-15. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of recreation visits to Yellowstone National Park in August 2026, as it will be reported in the National Park Service's official monthly visitation statistics.

target.what: Recreation visits to Yellowstone National Park as reported in the National Park Service's official monthly visitation statistics (NPS Visitor Use Statistics). A recreation visit is one person entering the park for recreational purposes; the same person entering multiple times on separate occasions c
target.publisher: National Park Service (NPS), Visitor Use Statistics program
target.cadence: Monthly, typically published with a lag of several weeks to a few months after the month ends
target.caveats: The target period is future relative to the 2026-08-15 cutoff; only partial August 2026 data (if any) would be available. The official NPS monthly report may be revised later. The definition counts visits, not unique visitors. Alternative interpretations include total recreational visits vs. total v

candidates.perspective: NPS official monthly visitation reports for Yellowstone
candidates.hypothesis: August is consistently the peak month for Yellowstone visitation. The August 2026 value can be estimated by applying the historical August-to-annual ratio or the recent year-over-year August growth rate to the most recent August data (August 2025) and any partial 2026 data available before the cutoff.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly recreation visits for Yellowstone for August 2015–2025, and any preliminary monthly data for 2026 (e.g., June, July 2026) published before 2026-08-15. Also annual totals for 2015–2025 to compute August share.

candidates.perspective: Entrance station counts and vehicle occupancy
candidates.hypothesis: Yellowstone has five entrances. August visits can be estimated from average daily vehicle entries × average persons per vehicle × days in August, adjusted for non-vehicle entries (e.g., pedestrians, cyclists). This route requires entrance count data or traffic counters.
candidates.data_to_find: Average daily vehicle entries at Yellowstone entrances in August (recent years), average occupancy per vehicle (from surveys or NPS reports), and number of days in August. If vehicle entry counts are unavailable, use total road traffic counts on approach highways as a proxy.
search_hints: average vehicle occupancy Yellowstone National Park

candidates.hypothesis: Overnight stays in Yellowstone (campgrounds, lodges, hotels in gateway towns) are a major component of visits. August visitation can be estimated from total overnight capacity × occupancy rate × average length of stay, plus day-use visits. This route requires lodging capacity and occupancy data.
candidates.data_to_find: Number of campsites, lodge rooms, and hotel rooms in Yellowstone and gateway communities; August occupancy rates for recent years; average length of stay for overnight visitors. If occupancy data are unavailable, use reservation data or park concessioner reports.
search_hints: gateway community hotel occupancy Yellowstone August

candidates.perspective: Closures, weather, and policy events affecting 2026
candidates.hypothesis: Any major closures (e.g., road construction, flood recovery, government shutdown) or unusual weather in August 2026 would alter visitation relative to historical patterns. Identifying such events and their expected impact can adjust the estimate from other routes.
candidates.data_to_find: News of Yellowstone closures, road closures, weather events, or policy changes announced before 2026-08-15 that affect August 2026 access. Also compare to 2022 flood impacts and recovery timeline.

candidates.hypothesis: Yellowstone visitation has a strong seasonal pattern with August as the peak. The year-over-year growth rate in August visits can be modeled from recent trends (e.g., 2023 vs 2024, 2024 vs 2025) and applied to the latest known August value. Alternatively, use the average August share of annual visits to project from a partial-year total.
candidates.data_to_find: August visitation for 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025; annual totals for those years; any 2026 year-to-date visitation through July 2026. Compute growth rates and seasonal shares.

candidates.perspective: Published forecasts or projections for Yellowstone visitation
candidates.hypothesis: Tourism forecasts, NPS planning documents, or economic outlooks for the Yellowstone region may include projected visitation for summer 2026. These can serve as a direct estimate or a sanity check.
candidates.data_to_find: Any published forecasts for Yellowstone visitation in 2026, including from NPS, tourism boards, or economic research firms. Also check for prediction markets or crowd forecasts for national park visitation.

candidates.perspective: Search and social media interest as a leading indicator
candidates.hypothesis: Online attention (Google Trends, social media mentions) for Yellowstone in the weeks before August 2026 may correlate with actual visitation. If a stable relationship exists between search volume and visits, it can provide a nowcast. However, this requires a validated bridge.
candidates.data_to_find: Google Trends data for 'Yellowstone National Park' for summer 2026 (available up to cutoff), and historical correlation with monthly visitation. Also social media post volumes if accessible.

assessment.note: All report the same July 2026 and July 2025 Yellowstone recreation-visit totals and the same ~2% year-over-year decline. They are repeated copies of one NPS measurement, not independent confirmations.
Repeated NPS year-to-date-through-July totals for 2021-2026. They establish the 2026 YTD level and the recent flat-to-slightly-down trend, but are duplicate vintages of the same series.
Repeated NPS August totals for 2021, 2024, and 2025. They are the only direct August observations and are internally consistent, but all come from the same NPS measurement.
Repeated NPS year-to-date-through-August totals for 2020-2025. They provide the historical August share of YTD and annual totals, but are duplicate vintages.
NPS 2014-2018 monthly averages and shares. They give a stable seasonal shape (August ~20.9% of annual visits) but are older-period context, not a 2026 level.

News-source annual totals for 2021, 2024, and 2025. They are rounded and differ slightly from NPS exact figures (e.g., 4.86M vs 4.8M for 2021), so they are contextual checks rather than precise inputs.

May 2026 was a record May with >570,000 visits, 20% above May 2021. This is a positive early-season signal that conflicts with the slightly negative July 2026 year-over-year change, suggesting August 2026 may not simply repeat the July decline.

2026 road-construction delays in Yellowstone (Canyon-West Thumb fiber project through Aug 14; Old Faithful area up to 15-minute delays mid-July to mid-August). These are modest, localized frictions that could slightly suppress August 2026 visitation relative to a no-construction counterfactual.

Yellowstone June 2025/2024 visits and overnight lodging stays, plus Old Faithful Snow Lodge August availability. They support a lodging-capacity route but are June-specific and do not directly give August 2026 visits.
Grand Canyon and Glacier June 2025/2024 visits and lodging stays. They are cross-park analogues for the lodging-to-visits relationship, not Yellowstone August data.
NPS-wide 2025 annual statistics. They provide system-wide context (323M visits, down 2.7%) but no Yellowstone August 2026 signal.

Yellowstone Google search lead over Grand Canyon and Jackson Hole enplanements up 4.36% in June 2026. These are attention/travel-demand indicators consistent with continued strong regional tourism, but no validated bridge to August visits is supplied.
2021 record-year context (busiest July, >4.8M annual visits). Useful as a high-water benchmark, but 2021 is an outlier year and not a direct 2026 predictor.
2022 flood and 2024 Biscuit Basin hydrothermal explosion. Historical disruptions that explain past anomalies but are not active in August 2026.

methods.rationale: Transfers the observed August 2025 level (p16 = 881,936) to August 2026 using a change factor (a1) centered near 0.99, reflecting the July 2026 year-over-year decline of 2% (p1, p14) tempered by the record May 2026 (p82) and only 1% YTD decline (p5). This is the most direct route because August 2025 is the latest observed August and the change factor captures the recent trend. Shared dependency: both p16 and a1 rely on the same NPS measurement system; failure mode is a structural break in August 2026 (e.g., new closure) not captured by the factor.

Estimates August 2026 as the product of a projected 2026 annual total (a3) and the August share of annual visits (a2). The annual total is anchored on 2025 (p74 = 4.76M) and 2024 (p75 = 4.74M) with a slight downward adjustment from the 1% YTD decline (p5); the August share is anchored on the NPS 2014-2018 average of 20.89% (p27). This route is independent of the August 2025 level and provides a structural cross-check. Failure mode: the seasonal share may have shifted, and the annual projection is uncertain.

Naive benchmark using the two most recent August observations (2025 and 2024) as a simple historical anchor. This ignores the 2026 trend but provides a low-information baseline for comparison. It is not expected to be the best estimate but helps calibrate the other methods.

methods.rationale: YoY transfer: August 2025 actual (p16) times an August 2026/August 2025 change factor (a1) anchored on the observed July 2026 -2% YoY (p1/p2) and YTD -1% (p5/p6). Shared dependency: both p16 and the July signal come from NPS monthly releases; failure mode is a structural break in August 2026 (new closure, weather, or demand shift) that decouples August from July.

Within-year seasonal transfer: July 2026 actual (p1) times the August/July ratio (a2), which is calibrated on 2021, 2024, 2025 August/July ratios (p16-p18, p2, p104-p105) and the 2014-2018 seasonal table (p26/p28). This avoids relying on the older 2014-2018 shares directly. Failure mode: 2026 road projects (p71-p73) or weather alter the July-to-August relationship.

Annual-share route: 2025 annual visits (p74, 4.76M) times the August share of annual visits (a3), calibrated on the 2014-2018 August share (p27) and the 2025 implied share (p16/p74). This is a cross-check on the monthly routes; failure mode is that 2026 annual visitation departs materially from 2025 or the seasonal distribution shifts.

Naive seasonal baseline: mean of the two most recent August values (2025 p16, 2024 p17), ignoring 2021's post-COVID peak. Provides a low-information anchor that the transfer methods should roughly bracket; failure mode is that it cannot capture 2026-specific demand or the road-project drag.

assumptions.name: August 2026 / August 2025 YoY change factor for Yellowstone recreation visits
assumptions.rationale: Anchored on the observed 2026 pattern: July 2026 was 2% below July 2025 (p1 vs p2) and YTD-through-July 2026 was ~1% below 2025 (p5 vs p6), while May 2026 set a record (p82). A modest decline of ~2% with wide uncertainty reflects the mixed signals and the 2026 road-project delays (p71-p73).
assumptions.applies_when: August 2026 demand tracks the July 2026 YoY decline and no major new closure or surge occurs.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a large August 2026 closure, a sharp demand surge, or a published preliminary August 2026 count far from this range.

assumptions.name: August 2026 / July 2026 ratio for Yellowstone recreation visits
assumptions.applies_when: The 2026 seasonal shape resembles recent years and no August-specific disruption changes the July-to-August relationship.
assumptions.falsified_by: A published August 2026 count implying a ratio outside this range, or evidence of an August-specific closure or event.

assumptions.name: August 2026 share of 2026 annual Yellowstone recreation visits
assumptions.rationale: August share of annual visits was 20.89% in 2014-2018 (p27); recent years show a slightly lower August share as the season lengthens (2025: 881,936/4,760,000 = 18.5%, p16/p74). A central 18.5% with wide bounds covers both.
assumptions.applies_when: 2026 annual visitation is near the recent 4.7-4.8M level and the seasonal distribution is stable.
assumptions.falsified_by: A 2026 annual total far from recent levels or a marked shift in the seasonal distribution.

methods.label: m1
methods.rationale: YoY transfer: August 2025 actual (p16) times an August 2026/August 2025 change factor (a1) anchored on the observed July 2026 -2% YoY (p1/p2) and YTD -1% (p5/p6). Shared dependency: both p16 and the July signal come from NPS monthly releases; failure mode is a structural break in August 2026 (new closure, weather, or demand shift) that decouples August from July.

methods.label: m2
methods.rationale: Within-year seasonal transfer: July 2026 actual (p1) times the August/July ratio (a2), which is calibrated on 2021, 2024, 2025 August/July ratios (p16-p18, p2, p104-p105) and the 2014-2018 seasonal table (p26/p28). This avoids relying on the older 2014-2018 shares directly. Failure mode: 2026 road projects (p71-p73) or weather alter the July-to-August relationship.

methods.label: m3
methods.rationale: Annual-share route: 2025 annual visits (p74, 4.76M) times the August share of annual visits (a3), calibrated on the 2014-2018 August share (p27) and the 2025 implied share (p16/p74). This is a cross-check on the monthly routes; failure mode is that 2026 annual visitation departs materially from 2025 or the seasonal distribution shifts.

methods.label: m4
methods.rationale: Naive seasonal baseline: mean of the two most recent August values (2025 p16, 2024 p17), ignoring 2021's post-COVID peak. Provides a low-information anchor that the transfer methods should roughly bracket; failure mode is that it cannot capture 2026-specific demand or the road-project drag.

kept.name: August 2026 / August 2025 YoY change factor for Yellowstone recreation visits
kept.rationale: Anchored on the observed 2026 pattern: July 2026 was 2% below July 2025 (p1 vs p2) and YTD-through-July 2026 was ~1% below 2025 (p5 vs p6), while May 2026 set a record (p82). A modest decline of ~2% with wide uncertainty reflects the mixed signals and the 2026 road-project delays (p71-p73).
kept.applies_when: August 2026 demand tracks the July 2026 YoY decline and no major new closure or surge occurs.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of a large August 2026 closure, a sharp demand surge, or a published preliminary August 2026 count far from this range.

kept.name: August 2026 / July 2026 ratio for Yellowstone recreation visits
kept.applies_when: The 2026 seasonal shape resembles recent years and no August-specific disruption changes the July-to-August relationship.
kept.falsified_by: A published August 2026 count implying a ratio outside this range, or evidence of an August-specific closure or event.

kept.name: August 2026 share of 2026 annual Yellowstone recreation visits
kept.rationale: August share of annual visits was 20.89% in 2014-2018 (p27); recent years show a slightly lower August share as the season lengthens (2025: 881,936/4,760,000 = 18.5%, p16/p74). A central 18.5% with wide bounds covers both.
kept.applies_when: 2026 annual visitation is near the recent 4.7-4.8M level and the seasonal distribution is stable.
kept.falsified_by: A 2026 annual total far from recent levels or a marked shift in the seasonal distribution.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
